title: Ceramide–niacinamide conjugate (NAM-Cer): a next-generation skin brightening active with reduced irritation and enhanced target affinity
content: Niacinamide (NAM) is a widely adopted multifunctional skincare active, whose clinical application is restricted by dose-associated skin irritation and insufficient target affinity. NAM-Cer (SuperCera N-nicotinamide (P)), a ceramide–niacinamide conjugate, was designed to attenuate NAM-mediated irritation while retaining and potentiating its brightening performance. A multiscale evaluation framework integrating in silico simulations (molecular docking and molecular dynamics), in vitro biological assays and a 28 day randomized clinical trial was implemented. Docking confirmed that NAM-Cer occupies binding pockets overlapping those of NAM and forms additional intermolecular interactions with TRPV1, IL-6, ELANE, MMP1, MITF and COL1A1, and MD simulations supported the stability of these binding complexes. Superior anti-inflammatory (IL-6, hBD-2), anti-irritant (TRPV1) and antimelanogenic activities, together with favorable biocompatibility, were observed for NAM-Cer relative to free NAM in vitro. Clinical data demonstrated that NAM-Cer retained skin-brightening efficacy against hyperpigmented spots and afforded superior skin tolerance compared with free NAM. These findings verify that ceramide conjugation circumvents the primary irritation drawback of conventional NAM while preserving its brightening property, supporting NAM-Cer as a safe and effective next-generation cosmetic active ingredient.
